added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own arms: baseline_suite (logs/baseline-suite.log, 0baeb0d40d, completed, 5 passed, EXIT=0) and after_suite (logs/head-gate.log, 5b6cefcbc8, completed, 6 passed, EXIT=0) both record zero failures, so no failure id is added by the change.

findings.text: the short-circuit branch calls read_plan_review(project, node.plan) with no plan=, so it selects the mtime-newest record for the plan rather than the newest covering record that plan_review.read_plan_review's own docstring and the else branch specify; with more than one stored review for a plan the launch can judge another section's findings, which is the same launch-versus-direct divergence the repair exists to close and is invisible to the tests because every fixture stores one review.

the section-match test duplicates queue_admission._contract_is_current (queue_admission.py:2521) line for line, and _contract_still_describes (routing.py:2642) repeats the digest comparison inside queue_admission._plan_review_owed (queue_admission.py:2700); routing.py already imports queue_admission lazily, so the checks could be factored into one owner rather than copied.

`launching` is inferred from `units is not None`, but queue_admission._dispatch_gate_owed (queue_admission.py:2599) also passes units explicitly for a queued request that recorded no contract, so that path can adopt a stale handover's contract for the same node and section and skip the coverage hold its own docstring says the full gate decides.

the done_when clause 'the test files importing reckon.crew.routing and reckon.crew.plan_review add no failures against the base revision' is still unestablished after the repair round; the only artifact is the aborted attempt-1 log, 20 lines with one F at 84%, no summary and no EXIT line, and neither manifest records an importer arm.
